worksheet.title: Read Bit's Stack
worksheet.subtitle: Run the blocks to find where Bit lands
worksheet.learning_goal: I can run a short stack and find where Bit lands.

parts.title: Run the stack
parts.text: Bit starts on box 1. Run the blocks from the TOP down, one at a time. Each ➡ block moves Bit one box to the right. Each ⬅ block moves Bit one box to the left. The star is on box 4.

parts.title: Where does Bit land?
parts.prompt: Run Stack 1 from box 1, one block at a time. Which box does Bit land on? Write the number.

parts.title: Land on the star
parts.prompt: Run Stack 2 from box 1. Which box does Bit land on? Is it the star? Write the number.

parts.title: You try — watch the last block
parts.prompt: Run Stack 3 from box 1. The last block is ⬅, so the last step goes back one box. Which box does Bit land on? Write the number.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: To know what a program does, you run it — one block at a time, in order. The same blocks in a different order land Bit on a different box.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Read Bit's Stack
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children run a short stack of blocks on a row of boxes and report where Bit lands. Running each block in order, one at a time, is running a program; the number and direction of blocks decide where Bit ends up. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper, a pencil, and a crayon. You read each prompt aloud. Optional: paper blocks (a green flag block + arrow blocks) to stack by hand, or floor boxes the child can walk.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Start on box 1; run each block top to bottom, moving one box per arrow.
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — Stack 1 (right, right) from box 1 lands on box 3.
3. Let them try. Children run Stack 2 (Ex 2) and Stack 3, where the last block goes back one (Ex 3).

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — Stack 1 (right, right) from box 1 → box 3. Exercise 2 — Stack 2 (right, right, right) → box 4, yes, the star.
Exercise 3 — Stack 3 (right, right, left) → box 3, then back to box 2. Bit lands on box 2.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: counting the start box as a step. The first arrow leaves box 1.
Make it easier: walk each stack on floor boxes, one step per block.
Make it harder: ask which stack lands Bit on box 5.
Make it active: a child is Bit and steps one box per block the class reads.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children carry out a sequence of coded instructions and determine the outcome.
In plain terms: running a stack of blocks in order to see where Bit lands.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child circles, numbers, or draws an arrow.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child runs each stack in order and writes the correct landing box.
